relations.subject: sgw:inter-sync-gateway-replication

relations.subject: sgw:inter-sync-gateway-replication
relations.evidence: Conflicts are only resolved during a **pull** replication. If conflicts occur, you should configure a `pushAndPull` replication.

notable_absence.finding: This is the sharpest contrast in the batch on the central ISGR/XDCR question. Conflict resolution is the ONE topic where a comparison to XDCR's own conflict-resolution vocabulary (xdcr:conflict-resolution-method - Sequence Number / Timestamp, bucket-level, fixed-at-creation) would be most natural to draw, and this page - the dedicated ISGR conflict-resolution reference - never mentions XDCR once. Its only explicit analogy target is Couchbase Lite (see relations above), not XDCR. Within this same five-page batch, overview.json's sibling page draws the XDCR parallel three times while this page, on the more XDCR-adjacent topic, draws it zero times. This asymmetry argues against reconciliation treating overview.json's XDCR mentions as establishing a settled pattern across ISGR documentation generally - they may be localized to that one page's 'Active-to-active Mobile Synchronization' framing rather than reflecting how the ISGR feature as a whole is documented relative to XDCR.

cross_component_finding: See notable_absence above: zero XDCR mentions on the page most likely to carry them, reinforcing round 27's original conclusion (drawn from configuration-schema-isgr.md's silence) even as overview.json (same batch) complicates it. Also notable: this page's 'Automatic Conflict Resolution' section (its own top section) is verbatim-identical to overview.json's '## Conflict Resolution' section - the same three paragraphs, same NOTE admonition, same footnote-style 'Alternatively' aside - meaning the two pages carry duplicate content with no cross-reference explaining which is canonical.
cross_product_finding: sgw:inter-sync-gateway-replication isAnalogousTo cbl:replication: the page states directly that ISGR's push/pull conflict-resolution asymmetry mirrors Couchbase Lite's own behavior, 'since in both instances Couchbase Lite is acting like the active node in an inter-sync gateway exchange' - a genuine, source-stated Sync-Gateway/Couchbase-Lite parallel, structurally distinct from (and not to be conflated with) the ISGR/XDCR question.
